punchline: Seagate's customers shrugged at its 3.5-inch prototype, so it was cancelled, and the same drive later cut into Seagate's own sales.
thirty_sec: Around 1985, Seagate built a working 3.5-inch drive and showed it to current customers, who were lukewarm. The program manager lowered his sales forecast and executives cancelled the project. Conner Peripherals shipped the same size of drive in 1987, aimed at portable computers. Seagate started making them in 1988 and sold to desktop makers, which cut into its own sales. Christensen uses it to show how sensible decisions can go wrong.
